Phoenix Sprinter Van Service With a Driver

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a Phoenix Sprinter van service that is chauffeured, not self-drive: you book the van and a professional driver together, and nobody in the group takes the wheel. 4 executive Sprinters serve the metro from this page. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is the entry point at $145 an hour on a 4-hour minimum, so an hourly charter starts at $580 before 8% tax — roughly $41 a seat. Above it sit the Maybach Sprinters. Below: every unit compared, what the rate includes, and how the quote is built. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

Is a Phoenix Sprinter van rental self-drive or chauffeured?

Chauffeured. Every Sprinter on this page is booked with a professional driver, and none of them is handed over on a key. 4 executive Sprinters serve the Phoenix metro today, from $145 to $295 an hour, each on a 4-hour minimum when you book by the hour. That distinction decides everything else. A self-drive rental gives you a van, a fuel gauge and a parking problem; an hourly charter gives you a driver who stages the vehicle, holds the wait between stops and owns the route. You are buying time on a vehicle, which is why it is priced per hour against a published minimum rather than per day. It also decides who can ride. A self-drive group is limited by who is on the rental agreement; here it is limited only by the seats — the Executive Black Sprinter takes 14, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter takes 8 — and nobody has to stay sober to drive home.

Which Phoenix Sprinter van rental with a driver is best for a group?

For most groups, the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter or the matching Executive White Sprinter, at $145 an hour on a 4-hour minimum; a smaller group that wants a Maybach books the 9-seat Maybach Jet Sprinter at $295 an hour or the 8-seat Maybach Shuttle Sprinter at $195 an hour. Seats run from 8 to 14, rates from $145 to $295 an hour, every unit shares the same 4-hour minimum, and the whole family is Mercedes-Benz. Every row here is forward-facing seating for a working ride — an airport run, a client visit, a team moving between offices. One routing note: a bachelorette, a birthday or a night out is a celebration booking rather than an executive one, and the 3 limo and party Sprinter cabins that serve it are marketed on the Scottsdale party bus rental page instead of here. Seats are published seated capacity — a limit, not a target. Bags are the cap the checkout counter enforces, read from the luggage line on that vehicle's own page; where no number is published the row says so instead of guessing. Starting total is the published hourly rate times the billable hours at that vehicle's minimum — the arithmetic the checkout runs. A longer day bills more hours, 8% Arizona tax sits on top, and per seat is that total divided by a full vehicle. What does a Phoenix Sprinter van service cost?

An hourly charter starts at $580 in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter — $145 an hour across the 4-hour minimum — before 8% tax. Split across a full vehicle that is about $41 a seat. The Maybach Jet Sprinter is the ceiling at $1,180. The same arithmetic runs for every unit. The Executive White Sprinter matches the black at $580; the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter opens at $780; the Maybach Jet Sprinter opens at $1,180. Those are the current published hourly rates and minimums, and what the booking flow charges against. A point-to-point transfer is the other product, priced as a trip with no hourly minimum — flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, priced from the drive beyond that with the empty return included, and usually cheaper for one airport run: $295 one way in the Executive Black Sprinter, $395 in the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter. Each extra stop on a transfer is $50; on an hourly charter the time is bought, so stops cost nothing. Payment follows the published deposit policy: pay 50% today by card and the balance is charged to that saved card 48 hours before pickup. Availability is specific to a date and a vehicle, so request a current quote with your date, hours and group size.

What is included in the hourly rate?

The vehicle, the chauffeur and the fuel, plus 8% Arizona tax at checkout and nothing else. There is no booking fee, no service charge and no fuel surcharge, gratuity is never added for you, and a day of 7 hours or more earns free hours against the bill. The inclusion list this company publishes on its corporate page applies to any chauffeured booking, and it is worth reading as written. "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked" "Tax only — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge, and gratuity never added for you" Two more are easy to miss. "Free hours as the day gets longer: 7–11 hours earns 1, 12–14 earns 2, 15 or more earns 3" — so a long Phoenix day costs less per hour than a short one. And on an airport leg: "Flight tracking on airport legs" The one on-board amenity is the plain one: "Bottled water on board, the one complimentary amenity on every ride" Not included: anything you add at checkout — a greeter, a child seat, hours past the booked window. The house rules are the same on every trip, and two are worth stating here: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." and "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

Which Phoenix trips do these Sprinters actually run?

Four shapes cover most of it: Sky Harbor arrivals and departures for a group, corporate movements between Phoenix offices and hotels, stadium and concert nights downtown, and day trips north. Each has its own page here, and each opens on the same 4 executive Sprinters rather than on a different fleet. Airport work is the biggest single use, and the airport page publishes the rule this page follows. "Give us the airline and flight number when you book. We track the flight. Stay together in baggage claim until your chauffeur sends the pickup instruction for your terminal, then move as one group. A greeter who meets you at baggage claim with a name sign and helps with your bags is an optional $200 add-on." On what to tell us: "Count bags, not just seats. Say up front if the group is carrying golf travel bags, ski bags or boxed gear, because those decide the vehicle more often than the headcount does." Corporate movements are the other steady pattern, and the reason the executive rows lead the table. A stadium or arena night downtown is the same booking on a different clock: one pickup, one wait, one ride home. Day trips north are long hourly charters, which is where the free-hour ladder matters most; Sedona and the Grand Canyon each have their own tour page.

Where in the Phoenix metro does a Sprinter pick up?

10 metro cities have a published service-area page, and a Sprinter reservation can start in any of them. Pickup is a street address rather than a zone, so a booking for 8 seats and one for 14 are quoted exactly the same way wherever the day begins. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. A day that starts in one city and ends in another is still one hourly charter: the clock runs from first pickup to last drop-off, and the drive between cities sits inside that window rather than on top of it. Because the charge is time rather than distance, a Phoenix address and a Scottsdale address cost the same per hour — what changes is how much of the clock the driving uses, which is the reason to list every stop up front.

Should you book this page or the Scottsdale Sprinter page?

Book by where the day starts. This page covers the Phoenix metro, Sky Harbor and Phoenix-side venues; the Scottsdale Sprinter van page covers Scottsdale. Both draw on the same 4 executive Sprinters at the same published rates, so the choice changes the itinerary and not the price. The two pages exist because the questions differ, not because the fleet does. A Phoenix booking usually starts at an airport, a downtown hotel or an office park; a Scottsdale booking starts at a resort. If the day crosses both, book it as one hourly charter: splitting a day across two bookings costs two minimums instead of one. Cancellation follows the published policy either way: a full refund 30 or more days out, the deposit kept between 14 and 30 days, and nothing refunded inside 14 days. The policies page prints the full text.

Things to know

  • Is this a self-drive Phoenix Sprinter rental? — No. Every Phoenix Sprinter request is for chauffeur-driven transportation. The selected vehicle, requested hours, route, and final terms are confirmed in writing.
  • What do Phoenix Sprinter vans cost? — The six published Sprinters currently show base rates from $165 to $275 per hour and vehicle minimums of two or three hours. Date, route, parking, tolls, overtime, and approved extras may affect the final written price.
  • How many passengers fit in a Phoenix Sprinter? — The published Sprinter options list passenger capacities from 10 to 16. Luggage, golf bags, accessibility equipment, and other gear may reduce the practical passenger fit and must be reviewed before confirmation.
  • Can I choose the exact Sprinter? — You can request a preferred published Sprinter and carry it into the booking flow. The assigned vehicle, seating configuration, finishes, amenities, and availability become final only when confirmed in writing.
  • Can the route include both Phoenix and Scottsdale? — Yes. Enter the full pickup, known stops, destination, requested end time, passengers, and luggage. The reservation team reviews access, timing, and route-specific costs before written confirmation.
